subject: Fan et al. (2023)
object: Fan et al. (2023) described 3 infertile women with female infertility characterized by oocyte maturation defects.

subject: Fan et al. (2023)
object: In 3 infertile women with oocyte maturation defects, Fan et al. (2023) identified homozygous missense variants in the CDC23 gene, a core subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C). One variant was c.986A-G (p.Tyr329Cys). In vitro experiments showed that this variant led to a decrease in CDC23 protein level.

subject: Fan et al. (2023)
object: Fan et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.988C-T (p.Arg330Cys) missense variant in the CDC23 gene in women with female infertility characterized by oocyte maturation defects. The variant changed the localization of CDC23 in HeLa cells and mouse oocytes.

subject: Fan et al. (2023)
object: Fan et al. (2023) found that Cdc23 Y329C/Y329C knockin mice mimicked the patients' phenotype. Their oocytes had low expression of CDC23 and APC4 and accumulated securin and cyclin B1. Treatment with AZ3146 rescued the phenotype.

subject: Cui et al. (2025)
object: Cui et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in infertile women from 639 unrelated Chinese families. They identified 3 probands carrying APC/C gene variants. The infertility in these families was characterized by disturbed oocyte maturation, fertilization failure, and arrest of early embryonic development.

subject: Cui et al. (2025)
object: In 2 unrelated Chinese women with infertility (cases 1 and 2), Cui et al. (2025) identified compound heterozygous missense variants in the CDC23 gene: c.A1277G, c.A833G, c.C182T, and c.C301T. The variants were found by whole-exome sequencing and followed a recessive inheritance pattern. The affected residues were conserved across species, and prediction programs (MutationTaster, SIFT, PolyPhen-2) suggested the variants were deleterious. In vitro studies suggested that the CDC23 variants caused dysregulated protein expression.

subject: Cui et al. (2025)
object: In an infertile Chinese woman (case 3), Cui et al. (2025) identified compound heterozygous variants in the APC13 (ANAPC13) gene: c.C6A and c.116_126del. The variants were found by whole-exome sequencing and followed a recessive pattern. In vitro studies suggested that the APC13 missense variant caused abnormal cellular localization of the protein. Structural modeling suggested that the APC/C variants may alter chemical bonds with other APC/C subunits.
